hero: At night in the emergency room of a provincial hospital in Nueva Ecija, a young Filipino medical intern empties an elderly farmer's plastic bag onto a steel tray: blister packs, loose white tablets, unlabeled capsules and a small bottle of brown herbal liquid, while a resident beside her checks a phone; the elderly patient lies on a stretcher with his daughter holding his hand; fluorescent light, focused mood; no text in the image.

figures.teaches: Kidney disease changes drug clearance, volume of distribution, protein binding and metabolite handling, so loading and maintenance doses are affected differently.
figures.content: A large basin labeled 'Volume of distribution' with water level labeled 'Drug concentration'. A faucet above labeled 'Dose (loading fills the basin; maintenance replaces what drains)'. Three drains at the bottom: 'Kidney' (narrowed, labeled 'falls with GFR'), 'Liver' and 'Gut wall' (partly narrowed, labeled 'uremia inhibits some enzymes and transporters'). Side callouts: 'Edema and ascites enlarge the basin for water-soluble drugs'; 'Low albumin and uremic toxins raise the free fraction'; 'Active metabolites cleared only by the kidney accumulate'. A dashed extra drain labeled 'Dialysis: removes small, water-soluble, weakly bound drugs with small volume of distribution'. Footer: 'Loading dose depends on volume; maintenance depends on clearance'.

figures.teaches: Sick-day rules need both hold and restart instructions.
figures.content: A wallet card, two sides. Side A title 'Sick-day plan'. 'Use when: vomiting, diarrhea, fever with sweating, not eating or drinking normally for a day'. 'Hold: metformin; SGLT2 inhibitor; ACE inhibitor or ARB; diuretic; any NSAID (pain reliever)'. 'Keep: insulin with more glucose checks; ask before stopping heart or transplant medicines'. Side B: 'Drink small amounts often; check glucose; watch urine'. 'Get help now: vomiting that does not stop, very little urine, drowsiness, fast breathing, glucose very high or very low'. 'Restart within 24-48 hours of eating and drinking normally, unless your doctor wrote otherwise'. Blank lines for 'My medicines (brand names)' and 'Restart date'. Small note 'Based on KDIGO 2024 practice points; consensus, not trial evidence'.
